question: Card seven of the vision on jaws-v1: Conspiracy Theorist (Human; on attack pay {1} and discard to draw; whenever you discard nonland cards, exile one from the graveyard and cast it this turn) in -- the pilot: 'the flashback on exiled spells is a way to return a wheel!!!! major advantage!' -- and for what?

contributions.slice: MODE prescribe: Theorist's cut; verbatim (it did not yet weigh a wheel cut, which the pilot opened mid-run)
contributions.text:
Conspiracy Theorist (013). Pick: in for Shark Typhoon (painful).
- Coverage: the goldfish lists it "seen" but no pattern reads the exile-and-cast clause; it sees at most a 2/2 that attacks and loots. The reason the pilot wants it is unread, so no rows.
- The wheel recast works on paper: Wheel of Fortune, Windfall, Reforge the Soul, Magus, Jace's Archivist and Collective Defiance discard; Echo of Eons, Time Reversal and Winds of Change shuffle instead. One card exiled per discard event, recast at full cost and normal timing (a sorcery wheel needs a main phase plus mana).
- With Library of Leng the choice is per card: a card Leng puts on top was still discarded (Theorist triggers) but cannot be exiled; send the wheel to recast to the graveyard and the rest to the top. Open for resolve-stack: Leng and Theorist's own pay-and-discard; the Wheel-then-exile-Windfall line.
- Combos: none of its Spellbook pieces is in the list; nothing live.
- Cost of cutting Typhoon: an instant-speed cycle (a Shabraz counter and a flying Shark), log 006's tutor target, and verified stack 012, which the cut orphans. In its place a 2-drop Human permanent: MV<=2 creatures 8 to 9.
- Second pick: Lizard Blades — orphans no stack, but the commander-damage group drops 4 to 3 and it is already an early permanent.
- Not cut: Unsettled Mariner (a changeling 2-drop Human). No wheel cut made — needs the pilot's word.

contributions.slice: MODE prescribe re-run with wheels open; verbatim
contributions.text:
Re-run with every rule lifted and wheels open: the same two swaps.
- Wheel screen, Winds of Change as the cut (goldfish, one instrument): finisher wheel by T8 -6.5 pts [-7.0, -6.0], damage @T10 -9.2 [-11.0, -7.4], wheels cast by T10 -0.38; better on dead wheels in hand (-0.022) and the keep rule (+2.7 pts) — partly backs "too many wheels", far outweighed. The Greatshark cut cost only 3.2 damage [-4.2, -2.1], no call on the finisher wheel.
- Pyromancer: on a competitive bracket-3 table a 3-mana repeatable answer that kills X/3s is worth more than a 5-mana counter that only stops creature and artifact spells.
- Theorist: Shark Typhoon is a 6-mana enchantment almost always cycled, in practice a spell; Theorist puts a 2-drop Human permanent in its place. Painful: an instant-speed draw that leaves a flying Shark, and stack 012 orphaned.
- If a wheel goes anyway: Time Reversal, not Winds — it shuffles (Theorist can never recur it), wipes the graveyard Theorist feeds from, costs 5. Judgment only, unmeasured; any wheel cut costs real finisher rate.
- Lizard Blades stays second choice for Theorist's slot; Unsettled Mariner stays.

call.pilot_words: no, shark typhoon stays! it's 6 mana, the hope is that I can get it in earlier with Treasure... I favor Conspiracy Theorist over Irencrag and would rather swap that for Voracious Greatshark than Irencrag, and consider something else for Irencrag
call.reading: Conspiracy Theorist in, for Voracious Greatshark rather than Shark Typhoon (Typhoon stays, the deck's namesake, cast early with Treasure); this takes the slot the previous study gave Irencrag Pyromancer, who comes out of it and needs a cut of his own.
